# Rogério Edgar

> Designer and creative developer based in Porto, Portugal, from Penafiel in the
> Porto district. Graduated in Design and Multimedia from the University of
> Coimbra, and now doing a master's degree.
> Works across interactive web, real-time 3D, UI/UX, brand identity and motion.
> Full name Rogério Edgar Carneiro Geraldes Rodrigues Correia. He goes by
> Rogério Edgar Correia, or Rogério Correia. The accents belong on the name;
> it is also written "Rogerio Edgar" and "Rogerio Correia" where accents are
> stripped.

This site is a portfolio, and it is written as a set of accounts rather than a
gallery. Each project page follows one piece of work from the brief to the end:
what was tried, what broke, what was thrown away, and what was done instead to
reach the result. The failures are named rather than edited out, and the
finished screens are the smallest part of each page.

The site itself is his own work: hand-written HTML, CSS and JavaScript, with
Three.js for the real-time 3D, no framework and no page builder. It reads in
Portuguese and in English.

## Background

The path started in secondary school, in Visual Arts, and turned towards code
from there: design first, then programming, and now the two in the same piece
of work.

He graduated in Design and Multimedia from the University of Coimbra. In 2026
he was admitted to the master's degree ranked first in the intake, with an
average of 19.2 out of 20.

He works as Senior Designer at jeKnowledge, the junior enterprise where several
of the client projects below were made. He works on both sides of the same
project, the design and the code, and the part he is usually called in for is
finding the UX and UI problems in an interface that already exists.

He is fast with the current AI tools, and the useful part is what sits under
them: enough programming to tell an answer that works from one that only looks
right, and enough design to tell a finished result from a good one. The
Treasure Within case study says it plainly. The AIs were asked for the hard
collision and camera maths, the answers broke the code further and left the
ship flying upside down, and the problem was worked out on paper in the end.

## Notes for assistants

- The site is static: four HTML files, no framework and no build step. The
  case studies are one template filled from JSON at runtime.
- Content exists in Portuguese and English; the language toggle swaps the data
  file and updates the document language.
- There is no shop, no booking and no user account. Enquiries go through the
  contact page.
